electric-gate-running-costs.title: Electric Gate Running Costs: Calculate Your Electricity Use
electric-gate-running-costs.description: Estimate annual gate electricity use from movement time, standby demand and your own electricity tariff.
sections: Measure two different loads

A gate uses electricity while moving and may also draw power while waiting. The controller, intercom, access receiver, network equipment and battery charger can contribute to that waiting load. Motor output ratings alone do not give the electricity drawn by the complete entrance.

Ask for measured input power or manufacturer consumption figures for the specified equipment. For two motors, use the combined demand. Record the total powered movement time for opening and closing, rather than treating an opening as a complete cycle.
A worked example with explicit units

This is an illustration, not a typical installation or a current tariff quote. Assume the complete system draws 100 W while moving and 5 W while idle. It makes ten complete cycles per day, each with 20 seconds of total powered movement.

Annual movement time = 20 × 10 × 365 ÷ 3,600 = 20.28 hours. Movement electricity = 0.100 kW × 20.28 hours = 2.03 kWh.

A 365-day year contains 8,760 hours. Idle time = 8,760 − 20.28 = 8,739.72 hours. Idle electricity = 0.005 kW × 8,739.72 hours = 43.70 kWh. Total electricity = 45.73 kWh. At an example tariff of £0.30 per kWh, that is £13.72 per year.
Adapt the calculation to your gate

Use annual kWh = (moving watts × moving hours + idle watts × idle hours) ÷ 1,000. Multiply the result by your unit tariff in pounds per kWh. Use 8,784 hours for a leap year.

The example treats moving power as the whole system demand during movement, so it subtracts movement time from idle time. If your motor figure is an additional load above a separately measured continuous baseline, calculate that baseline over the whole year instead. Do not count the same load twice.

If a cycle takes 40 seconds instead of 20, change the movement time before calculating both parts. Heaters, lighting and accessories that switch separately need their own power-and-time calculations.
Electricity is only part of ownership cost

SIM plans, cloud subscriptions, servicing, replacement batteries and repairs are separate costs. Ask which apply to the proposed equipment and whether VAT is included. An existing household electricity standing charge is not usually an additional gate cost; a separate metered supply could introduce one.

Keep electricity estimates separate from maintenance budgets when using our installed gate cost guide. For a retrofit, compare the work described in our automation quotation guide.
Compare running costs without confusing voltage and consumption

A label such as 24 V describes a voltage, not the annual electricity bill. Compare the input energy used by the complete installation and its actual operating pattern. If you are replacing equipment, ask whether the quoted consumption includes the controller, receiver, intercom and any backup charging.

Keep fixed ownership costs separate from electricity. A useful annual worksheet has distinct lines for energy, scheduled maintenance, connectivity or app services, and a repair allowance chosen for your own budget. Mark which amounts are quotations and which are assumptions. Do not turn a small calculated electricity cost into a claim that the entrance costs almost nothing to own.

If your household changes how it uses the gate, revise the cycle count and movement time in the example. If new always-on equipment is added, revise the idle demand too. Ask a competent person for suitable consumption information; do not open a control cabinet or insert an unsuitable measuring device to obtain it.
faqs: Is 100 W for 20 seconds, ten times a day, 20.3 kWh per year?
No. Under those assumptions it is about 2.03 kWh per year. Standby and other equipment must be calculated separately.
Is the example my likely bill?
No. Replace the sample power, operating time and tariff with figures for your own system.

winter-gate-maintenance.title: Winter Gate Maintenance for London Homes
winter-gate-maintenance.description: Prepare your entrance for wet and cold weather with safe observations, the right service records and a clear fault plan.
sections: Check the entrance before colder weather

From outside the movement area, look for damaged fittings, a leaning leaf, unusual gaps, standing water or debris near tracks and drains. Note changes in noise or movement during normal use. Do not repeat a faulty movement to investigate it.

Keep the gate instructions, service records and installer contact details together. Arrange an assessment before winter if the gate scrapes, hesitates or behaves differently. Tell the engineer about flooding, impact damage or recent paving work.
Keep homeowner care within the instructions

Carry out only the cleaning and care described for your installed system, using its stated isolation arrangements. Keep hands clear of hinges, rollers and trapping points. Do not remove electrical covers, change force settings or bypass sensors.

Lubricant type and application points depend on the equipment. Adding oil or grease to an unsuitable part can create problems. Ice, compacted debris and water in a motor enclosure need assessment; do not use force or improvised heat to restore operation.
What to discuss at a service visit

Ask the engineer to inspect the mechanical condition, supports, drainage, cabling and protective measures relevant to your entrance. Discuss how weather exposure and use affect the maintenance schedule. Request a record of findings, remedial work and checks before return to use.

Confirm the visit charge and what it covers before booking. Ask how parts or additional work will be authorised. A seasonal checklist cannot replace the maintenance instructions or an assessment of the complete system.
Prepare for a power cut or breakdown

Check that you have the correct user instructions and release key, and understand how the gate would be controlled and secured. Wind and gravity can move a released gate. Battery backup, where fitted, needs its own maintenance and capacity checks.

Read our manual-release guide before an emergency. If the motor hums without moving, stop repeated attempts and use our fault information checklist when requesting a repair assessment.

Further reading: HSE powered-gate safety and maintenance guidance.
Separate routine observations from repair work

SituationUseful homeowner informationWork to discuss with the engineer
A new scraping soundWhen it happens and whether the gate has changed position.Mechanical condition, alignment and the cause of contact.
Water after rainfallWhere water collects and when it disappears, observed from a safe place.Drainage, enclosures, connections and any affected equipment.
Intermittent openingWhich normal control was used and what response occurred.The relevant control route and complete gate behaviour.
Visible damagePhotographs from outside the movement area and known impact history.Stability, repairs and whether the gate should remain out of use.
Unknown service historyAvailable invoices, model details and handover documents.An initial assessment and a maintenance plan for the installation.

A checklist helps you describe changes; it is not permission to inspect moving parts. Keep observations brief and use what you have already noticed during normal use. If the gate is behaving dangerously, arrange help instead of collecting a better video of the fault.
Rain, leaves and underground equipment

Look at the whole entrance when discussing water problems. Tell the contractor about recent paving, blocked surface-water routes, new planting or a change in driveway levels. Photographs taken after rain can help explain where water gathers, provided you can take them without approaching exposed equipment or entering the movement area.

An underground operator may be out of sight, but its cover and maintenance access need to remain identifiable. Do not cover the area with planters, stored materials or a new surface without consulting the installer. Ask the engineer to check the drainage arrangement and explain what the owner may observe or clean under the supplied instructions.

Do not lift motor-box covers or bail water around electrical equipment as a general seasonal task. Report standing water and the symptoms you have seen. If the gate stops working after rain, tell the contractor whether other outdoor electrical equipment was affected, but leave electrical investigation to the appropriate competent person.

For leaves and debris, ask the installer to mark the areas the owner may safely maintain and the isolation steps that apply. A clear-looking track does not establish the condition of rollers, supports or equipment beneath a cover.
Frost and changes in movement

Report hesitation, unusual noise or a leaf that stops short instead of assuming cold weather explains it. Include the approximate weather conditions and whether the same behaviour occurred when the weather was milder. The engineer needs the actual model and condition to decide what to check.

Do not use boiling water, a blowtorch or another improvised heat source to free a gate. Avoid pulling on a powered leaf or repeatedly commanding it against ice or another obstruction. Follow the fault arrangements for the installation and keep people clear while access is restricted.

Ask for the specified care products and application points if the manufacturer permits owner lubrication. A general instruction to grease all hinges, tracks and racks ignores differences between systems. Keep the written instructions with the service record so a future owner does not inherit an unexplained bottle of lubricant and a guessed routine.
Book a service against an agreed scope

Give the contractor a list of changes since the previous visit. Mention building work, a vehicle striking the gate, replacement controls and any periods when the equipment was disconnected. Send the previous report so the engineer can see outstanding recommendations and parts already replaced.

Ask whether the quoted visit covers inspection only, routine servicing, adjustments, testing or fault diagnosis. Establish how additional work will be authorised and whether a further visit might be required for parts. Request the findings in writing rather than treating a service sticker as the complete record.

The maintenance interval should reflect the installed equipment and its use. A heavily used shared entrance and a lightly used private driveway need discussion on their own terms. Ask the contractor to explain its recommended interval and any circumstances that should prompt an earlier assessment.

Keep a simple owner log with the date, observed symptom, contractor contacted and outcome. Do not record guesses as confirmed diagnoses. For example, write that the gate stopped after heavy rain rather than declaring that the motor flooded unless the engineer has confirmed it.
Prepare the household for an interrupted entrance

Before poor weather arrives, check who has the instructions and knows whom to call. Keep the correct release key accessible to authorised users without storing it where visitors can misuse it. Ask for a demonstration at a service visit if you do not understand the documented procedure for your gate.

Discuss practical alternatives for arriving home, leaving for work and receiving deliveries while the gate is unavailable. A separate usable entrance can make a breakdown less disruptive. Do not rely on a courier or neighbour to improvise a release because they have used a different model before.

If backup power is fitted, ask what it supports, how its condition is checked and what happens when its capacity is exhausted. Record any warning indication the user should recognise. A working phone app does not establish that the motors have power or that the gate can move safely.

After a repair, ask what caused the problem, what changed and whether there is any revised owner care. Keep the new information beside the existing instructions. Seasonal preparation is most useful when it leaves the household with a clear access plan and a contractor with a reliable fault history.
After a storm or an impact

Check from a safe position whether the entrance looks different before returning to the usual routine. A fallen branch, leaning support or disturbed cable needs a report to the responsible contractor. Tell other household members about a restriction so somebody else does not operate the gate while you are arranging help.

Keep photographs and the timing of the event with the fault report. If another trade has been working nearby, share its description of the work with the gate engineer. Ask what must be repaired or checked before normal operation resumes, rather than assuming the absence of a visible obstruction resolves the problem.
faqs: Should every gate be serviced once a year?
Follow the system instructions and an engineer’s assessment of use, condition and exposure. A calendar interval alone does not establish that a gate is safe.
Can I increase the motor force in cold weather?
Do not change safety or force settings to overcome a fault. Stop using a gate that struggles and arrange assessment.

aluminium-vs-wooden-driveway-gates.title: Aluminium vs Wooden Driveway Gates
aluminium-vs-wooden-driveway-gates.description: Compare timber, painted aluminium and wood-effect finishes by appearance, construction, upkeep and complete installation scope.
sections: Compare samples at your property

Timber has natural grain and variation; painted aluminium gives a more uniform surface. Wood-effect aluminium offers a printed or applied timber appearance, but grain repetition, edges and the rear face can look different from real wood.

View samples beside your brickwork in daylight and shade. Ask to see the finish on a corner, joint and reverse face, rather than choosing from a small photograph. Check how the posts, pedestrian gate and fencing will match.
Look beyond the face of the gate

For timber, ask for the species or modified-wood product, board construction, frame joints and finish specification. For aluminium, ask about the frame, infill, joints, coating and repair options. The material name alone does not establish stiffness, durability or suitability for automation.

Solid boards and open bars create different privacy and wind-exposure conditions. Discuss weight, dimensions, supports and movement with the installer. Compare the complete gate design instead of assuming that one material will suit every opening.
Plan the upkeep you will accept

Timber coatings need care appropriate to the species, exposure and selected finish. Ask how to recognise when attention is due and whether you want the wood to retain its original colour. Aluminium still needs the specified cleaning, coating checks and maintenance of its fittings.

Separate the timber or coating warranty from the gate fabrication, installation and automation terms. Ask about exclusions, maintenance records and labour charges. A raw-material warranty does not promise that the complete gate will remain unchanged for that period.
Compare equivalent quotations

Put the same opening dimensions, infill, finish, supports, automation and access controls into both quotations. Include removal of the old entrance, power, groundworks, VAT and reinstatement. This gives you a useful comparison without relying on a universal lifespan or percentage saving.

Explore wooden driveway gates and aluminium gates. For modified timber, read our Accoya guide and ask for the proposed product terms. Then discuss your entrance.
A practical material comparison

DecisionTimberAluminium
AppearanceNatural grain and variation, with the chosen species, board pattern and finish.Painted or wood-effect finish, with profiles and joints that vary by range.
ConstructionAsk about the frame, joints, board fixing, moisture management and fittings.Ask about frame sections, infill attachment, joints, coating and fittings.
CareObtain the specified cleaning and coating care for the wood and exposure.Obtain cleaning, coating inspection and hardware care instructions.
Damage and repairsAsk how damaged boards, joints and finishes could be repaired.Ask whether panels can be replaced and how finish repairs are handled.
AutomationAssess the complete gate, dimensions, supports and operating geometry.Apply the same complete-system assessment to the proposed design.
WarrantySeparate timber, fabrication, finish, fittings and installation terms.Separate coating, fabrication, fittings and installation terms.

Use the matrix to compare actual products. The terms wooden and aluminium cover many constructions and finishes. Neither material name gives a reliable installed price, security rating or guaranteed service life for the complete entrance.
Choose the board pattern before deciding on colour

A full boarded surface, spaced slats and an open upper section give different views through the entrance. Look from the pavement towards the house and from the house towards approaching visitors. Decide what needs screening and where visibility remains useful. Compare the rear face too, because that is the view you may see most often.

Ask for a drawing showing board widths, spacing, frame edges and the relationship between the driveway gate and any pedestrian gate. A narrow side gate may use a different arrangement of boards even when the finish matches. Check whether those differences are acceptable before fabrication.

For wood-effect aluminium, request a sample large enough to reveal repeating grain and the treatment of corners and ends. For timber, ask what variation to expect between boards and what the selected finish will look like after weathering. A small online colour swatch cannot settle those decisions.

For a period property, start with its actual boundary details rather than a rule that every older house must have timber or ornate metalwork. Where controls apply, discuss the proposed material and appearance with the relevant adviser before ordering. A convincing timber effect does not itself establish planning acceptability.
Construction matters as much as the surface

Ask the fabricator to explain how the frame supports the infill and where the hinges or running gear attach. Request the details that matter for your chosen width and height. If automation is proposed, have the gate supplier and installer agree the arrangement instead of treating a motor kit as an unrelated addition.

Discuss solid infill and wind exposure together. A gate made from a lighter material still presents a surface to the wind, and the supports and equipment need assessment for the actual design. Avoid substituting an assumed material advantage for a measured specification.

Look for a written approach to drainage and moisture around joints, board ends and fittings. Ask how the selected hardware suits the material and exterior location. These questions help compare the proposed workmanship without assuming that every gate from one material has the same construction.

If you want to keep existing posts or brick piers, include their assessment in both material quotations. A change of leaf material does not establish that the old supports or hinges are suitable for the new entrance.
Budget for the upkeep you can realistically provide

Ask each supplier for a care sheet before you accept the quotation. It should identify the permitted cleaning products, coating inspections and any specialist work. Consider access to both faces of the gate, nearby planting and the time or contractor help you are willing to allow for upkeep.

Decide whether you want timber to retain a particular colour or are comfortable with the appearance allowed by the chosen finish system. Record that preference when discussing coatings. Do not rely on a universal recoating interval taken from another species, finish or exposure.

For a coated aluminium gate, ask how to deal with a scratch, damaged edge or impact. Establish whether the supplier offers repair materials, replacement boards or a refinishing service, and request terms rather than assuming those services are included. Hardware and automation still require their own care.

For both materials, keep cleaning and service records where the terms require them. Ask who deals with a problem involving more than one supplier, such as movement that damages a finish. A long material warranty and a practical route to resolving an installation problem are different things.
Compare three choices using the same entrance brief

If your priority is natural grain and you accept the specified care, compare suitable timber constructions and finishes. Ask about species or modified timber by name and request a sample of the proposed product. Include the fabrication and coating scope so the choice is more precise than wood versus metal.

If you prefer a uniform painted appearance, compare aluminium ranges against a painted timber alternative. Keep the infill, opening layout and finish colour consistent. Ask what changes at the joints, frame edges and reverse face; those details can explain why two apparently similar gates look different in person.

If you want a timber appearance with a different care routine, put wood-effect aluminium beside a real timber sample at the property. Make the decision in daylight and shade. Check the proposed posts and pedestrian gate at the same time so you are comparing a complete frontage.

Write down the non-negotiable requirements before requesting prices: usable opening, privacy, pedestrian access, acceptable upkeep and operation. Then compare the complete installed cost and written terms. You can choose on those practical differences without relying on invented lifespan figures or promises that any material needs no maintenance.
Ask what happens after accidental damage

Consider a vehicle scraping one panel or a fitting being damaged during building work. Ask whether an individual component can be replaced, whether the original finish can be matched and who would carry out the repair. Availability and matching depend on the actual product, so request a supported repair route rather than a guarantee that a later replacement will be invisible.

Keep the approved drawing, colour reference, sample details and invoice. These records help a repair contractor identify the supplied gate and give you a clearer comparison if you later replace a pedestrian gate or extend the adjoining fence.
faqs: Is aluminium maintenance-free?
No. Follow the cleaning and inspection instructions for the finish, hardware and automation.
Does wood-effect aluminium look identical to timber?
Compare full-size samples, joints and both faces in your own lighting. Finish systems differ and appearance is a personal choice.

swing-vs-sliding-gates.title: Swing vs Sliding Driveway Gates
swing-vs-sliding-gates.description: Compare parking clearance, side space, slopes and everyday access before choosing how your driveway gate opens.
sections: Measure the space each leaf occupies

A swing leaf travels around its hinge. For an illustrative pair of equal leaves across a 3.5 m opening, each leaf is about 1.75 m wide before allowing for gaps and fittings. Its free edge traces an arc with roughly that radius, rather than the full 3.5 m opening width.

That arithmetic is not a safe parking distance. Hinge position, opening angle, vehicle shape, pedestrian routes and protective clearances determine the usable space. Ask for a scaled plan showing the gate in motion and your car parked.
Allow for the full sliding arrangement

A sliding gate moves beside the entrance. The gate needs room along that path, including its supporting arrangement and safe separation from walls, fences and people. Cantilever designs have a supporting tail; tracked and multi-panel systems have different space requirements.

A car may be able to park beyond the sliding path, but the survey still needs to consider turning, waiting and pedestrian access. Read about telescopic options if side space is limited.
Slopes and drainage can change the choice

A rising driveway can obstruct a swing leaf. A sliding layout also needs a suitable travel path, supports and drainage. Neither layout becomes suitable simply by adding a stronger motor.

Share measured levels and any flooding history with the installer. Our sloping-driveway guide explains the questions to resolve before ordering.
Choose around daily use

Consider where visitors stop, how pedestrians enter, and how bins and deliveries pass the gate. Ask how you will operate the entrance during a power cut and what maintenance access the design needs.

Compare swing-gate installation with sliding-gate installation using the same design and access requirements. Groundworks and the complete specification determine cost; there is no fixed percentage difference that applies to every site.
Compare the layouts on the same drawing

Put both proposals on a plan showing the same opening, house, parking positions and boundary. Mark the gate closed, partway through its movement and fully open. Comparing only the open position can miss a conflict that occurs halfway through the cycle. Ask the surveyor to distinguish the structural opening from the clear space available to a vehicle after fittings and stops are installed.

QuestionSwing gatesSliding gates
Where does the gate go?Each leaf sweeps around its hinges into an agreed opening area.The panel travels sideways into a run-back area beside the entrance.
What must remain clear?The full arc, equipment and protective clearances, including when cars are parked.The whole travel path, supports, drive and protected run-back zone.
What site work matters?Suitable posts or piers, hinge geometry, levels and operator mounting.Suitable foundations and guides, plus the specified track or cantilever support.
What can make it awkward?A short parking bay, rising ground or a walking route through the swept area.A return wall, bin store, tree or another entrance occupying the storage side.
What should the quote show?Leaf sizes, opening direction, operator type and complete site work.Panel length, stored position, support design and complete site work.

Neither column supplies a minimum clearance. Use the table to identify the measurements that are missing from your quotation. A design that fits on an empty plan still needs checking against the way people actually use the property.
Three parking situations worth sketching

For a short driveway with parking straight ahead, show the rear or front of the car nearest the gate, including a tow bar or other projection. A swing layout may work if the vehicle can park beyond the complete swept area; a sliding layout may be worth comparing if that position is impractical. Do not turn the illustrative leaf-radius calculation into a parking instruction.

For two cars parked side by side, draw both vehicles and their doors open. A gate that avoids one car can still obstruct access beside the other. Show how somebody gets from each parking space to the front door without stepping into the moving gate area. Include the position used when unloading shopping or helping a child out.

For a narrow approach or tight turn, include the vehicle arriving from the street as well as its final parking position. A wider gate opening may help one part of the manoeuvre while leaving another corner constrained. Ask the surveyor to assess your actual vehicle and approach; a catalogue gate width alone cannot settle the turning question.

These are layout examples rather than surveyed installations. Bring photographs of normal parking to the appointment so the drawing reflects everyday use instead of an unusually tidy, empty driveway.
Wind exposure, privacy and the gate design

Discuss the amount of solid infill together with the location of the entrance. An exposed corner plot and a sheltered courtyard present different conditions. Give the installer information about strong gusts you have experienced, damage to earlier fittings and any planned removal of nearby screening. Ask how the proposed leaves, supports and operator suit that exposure.

Do not choose sliding solely because somebody calls it windproof, or fit a larger swing motor to compensate for unexplained resistance. The design needs to account for the complete assembly. A more open infill may deserve comparison where privacy requirements allow, but it still needs a site-specific assessment.

View the closed gate from inside and outside before committing to a privacy design. Consider visibility of visitors, headlights, the house frontage and any gap beside the stored sliding panel. Ask the drawing to show fencing or guarding required around the movement area, because those details also affect the finished appearance.
Plan walking access and breakdown arrangements

Decide whether pedestrians will use the vehicle entrance or a separate gate. Mark the intercom or keypad where a visitor can reach it without standing in the gate path. Show the route for a pushchair, wheelchair, bicycle and wheelie bin where relevant. A convenient vehicle opening can still leave an awkward daily walking route.

Ask the installer to explain access during a power cut or a mechanical fault before choosing the layout. Record who can operate the documented release, where instructions and keys will be kept, and how a released leaf will be controlled. A battery option should come with a defined supported configuration and maintenance arrangements.

For shared driveways, agree these arrangements with the people using the entrance. Discuss how work and future servicing can happen while residents still need access. Keep the access-control choice separate from the physical gate layout until both parts of the proposal have been checked together.
Compare installation and ownership costs

Ask both contractors to price an equivalent opening, finish and access-control brief. Separate gate fabrication, supports, operator equipment, power, excavation, drainage, protective measures and reinstatement. An inexpensive leaf can sit within a costly site project, while an existing suitable support or cable route may change the balance between proposals.

Record what each quotation excludes and which items remain allowances until inspection. Include waste removal, disruption to paving, access for installation equipment and any work by another trade. Ask who coordinates the finished levels if a driveway contractor is working at the same time.

Look beyond the initial total to the maintenance access, replacement-part support and finish care you are agreeing to. Request the service scope and written warranty terms for each proposal. There is no universal cost difference that makes one opening style the right choice for every London property.
Bring these details to a survey

Prepare photographs looking towards the gate and along both sides of the boundary. Add approximate opening dimensions, the usual parking arrangement and any planned change to the driveway. Identify drains, inspection covers and entrances that must remain accessible. Tell the surveyor whether you need a matching pedestrian gate, particular privacy or retained brick piers.

Ask for the recommended layout and at least one feasible alternative, with the reasons for rejecting any option that will not fit. Keep the resulting plan with the quotation so changes in panel size, supports or opening direction receive another check before manufacture.
faqs: Does a pair of gates need the entire opening width behind it?
Each leaf has its own swept arc. Use the actual leaf dimensions and a site drawing that also accounts for vehicles, people and protective clearances.
Which is better for a short driveway?
A sliding or folding design may help, but side space, supports, gradient and safe movement still need assessment.

automation-kit-installation-prices.title: The Cost of Automating Existing Driveway Gates
automation-kit-installation-prices.description: Build a retrofit budget that includes the gate assessment, supports, power, controls and completed-system checks.
sections: Check whether the existing gate can be automated

Start with the gate and supports, before choosing a motor kit. The survey should assess condition, hinges or running gear, movement, dimensions, exposure to wind and hazards around the opening. A manual gate that can be pushed by hand is not automatically ready for powered operation.

Ask whether the proposal needs repairs, altered supports, a different opening arrangement or replacement leaves. Include that work in the comparison with a new gate.
Separate the quotation into work packages

Request separate descriptions for gate repairs, motor and controls, power supply, cable routes, groundworks and surface reinstatement. Include access equipment, protective measures and any work by other trades.

Record VAT, removal and disposal, appointments, permissions and exclusions. A kit price covers a different scope from an installed and checked entrance. The cheapest motor listing cannot establish the completed project cost.
Specify operation and handover

Explain how often the gate operates, who uses it and whether you need pedestrian access, delivery entry or an intercom. Ask for the proposed product models and the basis for choosing them.

The quotation should identify completed-system checks, documentation, user instruction and manual-release training. Confirm maintenance, repair support and the separate equipment and installation warranty terms in writing.
Compare retrofit and replacement

If repair and alteration costs are substantial, request a replacement option with equivalent appearance and controls. Compare the complete scope, disruption and upkeep rather than assuming retrofit must be cheaper.

Use the installed gate cost guide alongside our gate automation service. Send photographs, approximate dimensions and known faults when you discuss your entrance.

Further reading: HSE guidance on complete-system assessment.
Compare surface-mounted and underground operators

The operator type affects both the appearance of the gate and the installation work. Compare an above-ground linear or articulated-arm proposal with an underground proposal using the actual hinge and support arrangement. Ask for a drawing showing mounting positions, movement and access for servicing. Product names alone do not establish that either arrangement will fit.

OptionWork to establishQuestions for the quotation
Above-ground linear armMounting geometry on the leaf and support, brackets, cable route and movement clearance.Can suitable fixings be made to the existing structure, and what alterations are included?
Above-ground articulated armSpace for the linked arm and suitable mounting on the support and gate.Where does the mechanism move, and how will the surrounding area be assessed?
Underground operatorFoundation box, hinge relationship, excavation, drainage, cables and access to covers.Who provides drainage and reinstates the driveway, and what remains visible?
Existing sliding gate driveCondition of the gate, running gear, supports and compatible drive arrangement.Which existing parts can remain and what needs repair before automation?

Above-ground equipment can still require groundworks for supports or cables. Underground equipment can still leave covers and release fittings visible. Compare the documented site work rather than treating one option as excavation-free or the other as completely invisible.
Identify what a motor kit actually includes

Ask for a component list tied to the supplier and model numbers. Depending on the offer, a kit may include operators, a controller, receivers or selected accessories. It may exclude the equipment and work needed to make your particular entrance suitable. Have the installer mark supplied, retained and separately priced items on the same list.

A pair of existing manual gates also needs consideration as a structure and as a moving entrance. Photograph the hinges, supports and gate from safe positions, and send the approximate leaf dimensions. Tell the contractor about sagging, rubbing, repairs or occasions when wind moved a leaf unexpectedly.

Do not use a catalogue maximum weight as the only selection rule. Ask the contractor how the proposed equipment suits the gate dimensions, mounting geometry, infill, exposure and operating demand. The answer should identify the equipment being priced, not just promise a powerful motor.
Power routes and driveway work can change the budget

Draw the approximate route from the entrance towards the available supply and flag finished paving, steps, walls, trees and inspection covers along it. The electrician and gate installer need to establish the actual electrical requirements and cable route. A photograph can help an initial discussion but cannot confirm the condition or suitability of the supply.

If you plan a new driveway, agree ducts, foundations and finished levels before the paving programme starts. Name who provides each part of the work and who checks the interfaces between trades. Include making good even where an existing route may be reusable; the quote should say what happens if inspection finds that it cannot be used.

For underground operators, request a specific drainage proposal for the site. Ask how covers remain accessible after resurfacing and how future equipment replacement would be approached. These are ownership questions as well as installation costs, because the cheapest initial arrangement may be inconvenient to maintain.
Use a quotation worksheet instead of a generic price band

Create one row for each work package and one column for each proposal. Copy the contractor’s description and price into the worksheet without converting an allowance into a fixed amount. Leave an item marked not stated until the contractor clarifies it. That makes omissions visible before a deposit is agreed.

Separate the base installation from choices such as a different intercom, extra remotes or an additional pedestrian entrance. Record ongoing charges beside the features they support. A smartphone option may involve different ownership and connectivity arrangements from a fixed indoor answering point.

Check payment stages, quotation validity, VAT treatment and how variations require approval. Ask what happens if concealed damage or unsuitable foundations emerge after work starts. Avoid assuming an advertised equipment price includes fitting, electrical work, disposal or complete-system checks.

Where two proposals differ materially, ask for a comparable alternative rather than negotiating an unexplained total. A contractor who includes replacing damaged supports is pricing a different job from one who assumes that the existing supports can remain.
Three retrofit scopes to discuss with the installer

For sound gates with suitable supports, the main question may be the operator arrangement and the work needed to connect, protect and commission the entrance. Ask the installer to confirm the condition and list retained components. Treat this as a possible scope, not an assurance that your own manual gates are ready.

For gates that sag or scrape, separate the repair proposal from automation. Ask what the repair would achieve, how the result would be assessed and whether further alterations remain necessary. A motor should not become the explanation for forcing a poorly moving gate through its travel.

For an entrance that needs major support work and new controls, compare a complete replacement using an equivalent design brief. Retaining the leaves may still be worthwhile for appearance or conservation reasons, but the quotation should show the cost and limitations of that choice.

These examples explain why a useful budget begins with a scope. Once the contractor has surveyed your gate, request a written proposal you can compare against the alternative, with the same finish, controls, safe operation and handover requirements.
Agree the changeover day

Ask how long the entrance is expected to be unavailable and where vehicles should be parked during the work. Confirm access for residents, pedestrians and deliveries, especially if the gate is the only entrance. Programme electrical and driveway work around the installation rather than leaving responsibility unclear between contractors.

Before paying the final balance under your agreed terms, request the documented checks, user instructions and demonstration included in the quotation. Identify who will deal with any incomplete item and when it is expected to be resolved. Keep model numbers, settings records supplied for the owner and warranty documents together.

If the installer discovers work outside the agreed scope, request the reason, revised price and effect on the programme before authorising it. That is more useful than trying to compare an unexpectedly enlarged retrofit with an earlier equipment-only estimate.
faqs: Can you give a fixed retrofit price from a motor model?
A motor model does not identify the repairs, power, groundworks or protective measures needed. A site assessment establishes the complete scope.
Can I keep my existing controls?
Compatibility and condition need checking against the proposed equipment. Identify retained parts and any limitations in the quotation.

best-intercom-systems.title: Choosing an Intercom for Your Driveway Gate
best-intercom-systems.description: Compare audio, video, wired, IP and GSM gate intercoms, including retrofit compatibility, smartphone access, installation costs and handover checks.
sections: Decide where you want to answer visitors

List who should receive a call and whether they need an indoor monitor, phone calls, an app or a combination. Include anyone who does not use a smartphone. Decide what happens if nobody answers and how a visitor can leave a delivery.

Ask for a demonstration of the actual sequence: call, identify the visitor, grant entry and confirm that the gate has finished moving. Seeing a video does not necessarily mean the app reports the gate’s physical position.
Audio or video: choose the visitor information you need

An audio intercom lets you speak to the visitor. A video intercom adds a view from its camera. Decide whether a conversation is enough for your entrance or whether you need to see a caller before granting access. Consider household members who find a small screen, quiet speaker or app notification difficult to use.

For video, ask to see the view from the proposed mounting position. A camera aimed at a driver may not give the same view of someone on foot. Discuss lighting after dark, glare, weather exposure and the position of a caller using a wheelchair. A specification such as camera resolution cannot answer those layout questions.

Decide whether you want live viewing only or recordings, missed-call images and notifications. Have the supplier identify which features the proposed configuration provides and any storage or subscription requirements. Avoid assuming that video entry automatically includes recording or confirms the position of the gate.
Wired, IP and mobile intercoms: compare the whole route

Separate the connection between gate and house from the method used to answer a call. A system can have wired components and still use an app for some functions. Conversely, a wireless call path does not remove the need to supply and connect the equipment at the entrance.

OptionWhen to consider itConfirm before ordering
Dedicated wired indoor answeringYou want a fixed handset or monitor for use at home.Cable condition and route, compatible indoor units and whether local calls need any network service.
IP or app-based answeringYou want supported network features or calls on selected phones.Network coverage, account ownership, app support and which functions depend on an internet or cloud service.
Mobile-network entryA suitable cellular service offers a practical call path at the entrance.Device and SIM compatibility, voice or data requirements, signal and recurring charges.

Some products combine indoor answering with phone access. Have the installer explain the configuration, including what still works if one connection fails. Calling a system hardwired does not establish that all of its features operate without the internet.
Compare the connection paths

A wired indoor system can suit a household that wants a dedicated answering point. An IP system needs the specified network and power arrangements. A mobile-network intercom needs suitable coverage, device support and a compatible SIM plan.

Test the connection at the proposed gate position. A strong indoor Wi-Fi signal or a phone signal from another network does not prove the intercom will work there. Discuss what remains available during a broadband, mobile-service or power failure.
Smartphone apps and smart-home integration

Write down the devices your household uses and the actions you need: answer a visitor, view the entrance, request opening or receive a missed-call notification. Ask the installer to demonstrate those actions on the proposed equipment. Support for one action does not establish support for all the others.

The Comelit app documentation, for example, lists entrance-panel calls and gate release among its functions, with manuals for named video-entry devices. Ask which functions the quoted hardware supports. That is why a brand name or an app logo is not enough to confirm compatibility with an existing installation.

For Ring, Google Home, Control4 or another existing system, use our smart-home integration checklist to define the exact functions and equipment. Confirm who supports the connection after an update and how account access transfers when you change phone or sell the property. Do not assume a general-purpose video doorbell includes a supported gate-release interface.
Retrofit an intercom without replacing the whole entrance

Start with the controller, existing answering equipment and any cable records. Ask the contractor to inspect the available route, supply and release connection. Reusing a cable or indoor monitor may be possible with a compatible system, but the proposal should identify the equipment it intends to keep and any limitations.

Tell the contractor whether you need full vehicle entry, pedestrian access or a separate pedestrian gate. Describe how each entrance should respond rather than asking for an extra relay without explaining its purpose. The team needs to assess the command interface alongside the safe operation of the gates.

If the current intercom rings but the gate does not open, record that symptom before deciding to replace the intercom. The calling function and release function need separate assessment. Buying a new entrance panel may not resolve a fault elsewhere in the system. This buying guide cannot diagnose that fault from the ringing sound alone.
Get the exact equipment and account terms

Request model numbers, the proposed release interface, supported monitors and app requirements. Confirm recording options, retention, subscriptions, SIM charges and which account owns the system. Ask how to remove a former resident or contractor.

Product families contain different devices. Compare named configurations rather than assuming a brand guarantees compatibility. Our Comelit and Hikvision comparison shows why the component list matters.
Compare installation costs and ongoing commitments

A useful quotation names the entrance panel, camera if required, indoor answering devices, power equipment and connection to the gate. It also describes cable work, mounting, network setup, configuration, testing and reinstatement. Ask whether VAT is included and which items depend on the site survey.

Compare recurring costs on the same basis. List SIM charges, subscriptions, recording or cloud-storage plans and any paid support. Confirm what happens to each function if a subscription ends. Ask the supplier to distinguish equipment warranty from installation workmanship and explain how future visits will be charged.

There is no sound universal fitted price for every London entrance. An existing usable cable route and a new route through finished paving involve different work. For a meaningful comparison, send each contractor the same brief and request the same answering points and access functions, rather than comparing only the price of the outdoor panel.
Shared entrances, recordings and control of accounts

For flats or a shared driveway, specify which household receives each call and who manages changes when residents move. Ask how visitors find the right name and how delivery access will work. Confirm the proposed capacity, user permissions and any management charges for the particular configuration.

If recording is proposed, discuss the camera view, whether audio is recorded, who can view footage, where it is stored and how long it is retained. Avoid treating a camera as permission to record neighbouring property without considering privacy. Agree the appropriate arrangements for the actual site before enabling recording.

Keep the property owner or responsible managing agent in control of administrator access and recovery details. Ask for a demonstration of removing a former resident without disrupting everyone else. Include residents who prefer a fixed answering point or cannot rely on a smartphone in the requirements from the start.
Plan installation and support

Include cable routes, power, camera position, lighting, accessibility and weather exposure in the survey. Confirm who commissions the connection to the gate controller and checks operation of the complete entrance.

Compare video intercoms and phone entry. Check Ofcom’s network-retirement guidance before buying mobile-network equipment.
A handover demonstration worth asking for

Use the visitor journey to check the installation with the contractor: a person arrives at the intended calling position, selects the right household, makes contact and receives a response. Then confirm the authorised release action and how users should observe or verify the entrance. Keep people outside the movement area during the demonstration.

  • Check conversation quality and, where fitted, the camera view in the agreed conditions.
  • Demonstrate calls to each specified monitor or phone, including the unanswered-call arrangement.
  • Explain which functions depend on power, broadband, mobile service or an active account.
  • Show user management and provide the correct equipment instructions.
  • Record support contacts, renewal responsibilities and the agreed fallback access.

A successful video call does not prove the whole powered gate is safe. The installer needs to check the completed entrance and its protective measures. Ask for the handover records and maintenance advice, and keep them accessible to the person responsible for the property.
faqs: Which brand is best?
Compare the proposed models against your wiring, visitor workflow, network, account costs and support requirements. A brand ranking cannot establish compatibility.
Does an app continue working during a power cut?
That depends on backup power for the gate, intercom and network equipment, as well as the service connection. Ask for the actual failure arrangements.
Can I keep an indoor monitor and answer on my phone?

Some compatible configurations provide both. Ask for the exact monitor, network or gateway equipment, app requirements and unanswered-call behaviour rather than assuming every product in a range supports them.
Can an intercom be fitted to my existing gates?

A contractor needs to assess the gate controller, command interface, power and cable arrangements. Existing components may be reusable, but a universal retrofit promise would not establish compatibility.
Will a video intercom show whether the gate is closed?
A camera view and a gate-position signal are different features. Ask how the proposed system establishes and displays the actual gate state; do not assume an opening command confirms movement.

gsm-gate-openers-london.title: GSM Gate Openers: Network, SIM and Access Checks
gsm-gate-openers-london.description: Compare GSM gate openers for London homes: SIM and 4G compatibility, signal surveys, retrofit requirements, access permissions and ongoing costs.
sections: Separate phone entry from visitor calling

Some gate controllers recognise an authorised phone number and request an opening when it calls. An intercom also lets a visitor speak to a resident. Ask which function the proposed device provides, whether it uses voice, SMS or data, and what the caller experiences.

A remote command does not confirm that the entrance is clear or the gate has opened. Discuss how the complete system manages unattended operation and how you will know whether a fault has prevented movement.
How a SIM-card gate opener differs from an intercom

With a phone-operated gate switch, an authorised user contacts the number or service assigned to the installed device. The unit then requests an action from the gate controller. An installer needs to confirm the supported method, permissions and controller connection for the chosen model. You should not assume that dialling any gate SIM number grants access.

The AES i-Gate product information, for example, describes call and SMS control of its GSM switches. Its products and app arrangements vary, so specify the exact model rather than asking for an unspecified GSM box. A gate switch does not by itself give a visitor a microphone, camera or call button.

If you want a delivery driver to call you from the gate, specify that visitor conversation separately. Decide whether you need audio or video and how you want to answer. A cellular video system may use a data connection and an app, while another unit may place an ordinary voice call. Confirm the actual call path during the quotation stage.
Check the device, SIM and network together

Ask for the exact device model and supported network technologies. Confirm the SIM plan permits its required services and how the unit handles caller identification. A label saying 4G does not, by itself, confirm support for the voice service your network uses.

As checked in October 2026, Ofcom reports that UK 3G networks have switched off and that operators are preparing their 2G closures. Check Ofcom’s current switch-off guidance and obtain the equipment supplier’s migration advice. Avoid buying an older controller solely because a SIM currently connects.
Signal at the entrance: check the installation position

A postcode coverage result is a starting point for the survey, not an acceptance test for the finished installation. Ask the installer to check the proposed network at the intended unit and antenna positions. Give them the location of the gate relative to the house, boundary walls and any existing equipment enclosure.

On a London mews or recessed entrance, describe the physical layout instead of assuming that a city address guarantees coverage. The installer should explain how the antenna and cable route will suit the product. Do not run an antenna cable through a motor housing or move electrical equipment yourself to improve reception.

Agree how the team will demonstrate successful calls or commands after installation. Test the functions you bought from the places you expect to use them, under the agreed safe operating arrangements. Keep a record of any unresolved reception problem rather than accepting an occasional successful command as the whole handover.
Can phone entry be added to existing electric gates?

A retrofit needs a compatibility assessment of the existing gate controller and the proposed entry device. Provide the controller details from your records and explain which remotes, keypads, intercoms or pedestrian controls you want to retain. The installer should identify the command interface and power arrangements before quoting the connection work.

Ask whether the new control will request full opening, pedestrian access or another configured action, and how that fits the current operation. A phone module does not repair an unreliable motor or make a defective entrance safe. Any wider fault needs its own assessment.

Discuss adding GSM phone entry with the equipment list and photographs taken from safe positions. Confirm who will install, configure and check the completed system. Avoid a universal wiring diagram or SMS command copied from a different product manual.
Survey the signal and ongoing costs

Test service at the gate position on the proposed network. Discuss the enclosure, antenna location, cable route and power supply with the installer. Nearby buildings and the installed position can affect the result.

Confirm monthly charges, call or data allowances, top-up rules and what happens if an account expires. Ask whose name holds the SIM and how the household can change numbers or recover administrator access.
Purchase price, SIM charges and the cost of ownership

Compare quotations for the complete installation. List the controller or intercom, antenna, power provision, wiring, mounting, configuration and handover. If existing cable or power provision can be reused, ask the contractor to state that assumption and what happens if the survey finds it unsuitable.

Ask for the recurring charges in a separate line: SIM rental or top-ups, outgoing calls, texts, data and any app or service subscription. Establish which functions need each service. A device that uses calls for entry can have different requirements from one that sends video to an app. Neither the GSM label nor an app-store download establishes that ongoing use is free.

Keep a note of the renewal date and the person responsible for payment. For a shared entrance, agree how residents will fund the service and who can speak to the provider. You can then compare options over the same period without relying on a claimed universal saving.
Authorised users, visitors and shared-driveway access

Decide who should open the gate without speaking to a resident, who should receive visitor calls and who may change permissions. These can be different groups. Ask the supplier to demonstrate the permissions on the proposed model, including how to remove a lost phone or a former resident.

If you want time-limited visitor access, verify that the particular product and configuration support it. Agree who creates that access and what happens at expiry. Do not assume that every phone opener provides temporary codes, access logs, schedules or gate-position feedback. Those are features to confirm in writing.

Keep administrator credentials separate from everyday entry arrangements. Follow the product instructions to replace default credentials where applicable, and agree an account-recovery process that the property owner or managing agent controls. Avoid leaving the entire installation tied to the private account of a departed installer.
Hand over access management

Request a demonstration of adding and removing authorised users using the actual manual. Remove default credentials, restrict administrator access and arrange a backup entry method. Keep account recovery information with your gate records.

Compare visitor workflows in our intercom guide. A failing controller belongs in a repair assessment rather than a generic SMS reset sequence.
Loss of service, missed calls and handover checks

Ask what remains available if the mobile service fails, the SIM account expires or the gate loses power. Retained remotes or a keypad may offer another command method where the gate system remains operational; they cannot overcome every power or mechanical fault. A backup battery has a particular capacity and maintenance requirement, not a guaranteed number of days of access.

If phone entry stops working, note whether ordinary gate controls still work, which callers are affected and what the caller hears. Check the account status through the provider or responsible administrator. Give the installer that information without opening the unit or resetting its stored users. A failed call and an accepted call with no gate movement need different investigations.

  1. Demonstrate resident entry and visitor calling if both were specified.
  2. Confirm the intended gate action and explain any status message or notification.
  3. Demonstrate adding and removing an authorised user using the correct instructions.
  4. Record the SIM owner, payment arrangements, model details and support contact.
  5. Explain fallback access and the circumstances in which the entrance must remain out of use.

Keep that record with the gate documentation so another authorised person can manage the system later. Review permissions when occupants or regular contractors change, rather than waiting for an access problem.
faqs: Will any UK SIM work?
No universal compatibility claim is reliable. Check the device, network, required voice/SMS/data services and tariff restrictions together.
Do I need Wi-Fi at the gate?

A mobile-network device can use a compatible SIM service instead of a home Wi-Fi connection. Confirm the chosen model, signal, power supply and required voice or data services; other entry devices may use Wi-Fi.
Can I open the gate from abroad?

Ask the supplier and mobile provider about the chosen command method, international calling or roaming restrictions and charges. Remote access also depends on the installed system being operational and suitable for unattended commands.
Does a GSM opener include video calling?
Not necessarily. A phone-operated switch, an audio intercom and a cellular video intercom provide different functions. Specify visitor calling and video if you need them.

telescopic-gates-space-saving-london.title: Telescopic Driveway Gates for Limited Side Space
telescopic-gates-space-saving-london.description: Considering telescopic driveway gates? Compare panel layouts, side-space measurements, groundworks, maintenance and the questions to include in your quotation.
sections: How telescopic driveway gates work

Telescopic driveway gates use two or more sliding panels that overlap as they open. The arrangement can fit an entrance where a single long sliding leaf would have too little room beside the opening. You still need space for the stored panels, their supports and the full movement of the mechanism.

Picture the entrance from above: the panels move along neighbouring paths and gather beside the driveway. The installer must show how the selected system coordinates them. A photograph of closed gates will not tell you the stored width, depth or position of the equipment behind them.

A manufacturer example helps explain the difference between systems. Comunello’s Ranger mechanism uses a ground-fixed toothed track and special wheels coupled to racks on the gate. That describes one engineered arrangement, rather than a specification for every telescopic gate. The proposed hardware and drawings should match each other.
Measure the opening and the space beside it

Start with a sketch that records your clear entrance width and the available strip beside the gate. Label the inside and outside of the property so the contractor can understand where the panels would gather. Use approximate dimensions for an initial enquiry; the installer needs a measured survey before confirming the design.

The opening width alone cannot establish whether telescopic gates fit. Panel overlaps, guide supports, stops, guarding and maintenance access affect the space required. A claim that the system needs a fixed percentage of the entrance width is too broad without the selected product and layout.

  • Clear vehicle opening: measure between the parts that will remain in place, allowing the survey to establish the final usable opening.
  • Side length: show where a wall, tree, building corner or other obstruction ends the available run-back area.
  • Stored depth: identify how far the overlapping panels and equipment project into the property.
  • Levels: note changes across the opening and along the proposed panel path.
  • Other access: mark bins, meter cupboards, drains and any route people need to use beside the gate.

Include photographs looking along the boundary as well as towards the entrance. A straight-on photograph can hide a shallow return wall or a parked vehicle behind the proposed storage area.
Compare telescopic gates with other layouts

LayoutSpace to establishDecision to make
Single-leaf slidingThe complete run-back length and support arrangement beside the entrance.Whether one leaf can clear the opening without blocking other access.
Telescopic slidingLength and depth occupied by the overlapping panels, guides and protective measures.Whether the compact storage arrangement justifies the additional mechanism and upkeep.
Bi-foldThe whole folding and swinging path, including where panels gather.Whether parked vehicles and people can stay clear throughout movement.
Conventional swingThe arc of each leaf and its clearance above the driveway.Whether the parking position and levels leave a workable opening path.

Compare drawings at the same scale with the same vehicle position. Our bi-fold and sliding gate comparison covers the alternative movement paths. A smaller-looking gate can still obstruct a useful part of a short driveway.

For example, imagine an entrance with room beside it for overlapping panels, but a bin store directly behind that space. The telescopic layout may help vehicle access while making bin collection awkward. Moving the bin store, changing the storage side or choosing another arrangement would all deserve consideration. This is a planning example, not a clearance recommendation.
Tracks, supports, drainage and finished paving

Have the quotation identify how each panel carries its weight and stays guided through its travel. The contractor should distinguish tracks at ground level from supporting frames or other arrangements in the proposed design. Terms such as telescopic, tracked and cantilever describe different aspects of a gate; they do not establish an interchangeable set of parts.

Ask for a drawing of the foundations, track or support positions and the finished driveway levels. Identify drains and inspection covers before agreeing where the mechanism will sit. The installation team should explain how it will keep access to anything that needs inspection or maintenance.

Coordinate this work with any new driveway surfacing. Agree who sets the levels, installs ducts, manages drainage and reinstates disturbed paving. A quote that leaves those tasks to another contractor can appear cheaper while covering less work. For the broader installation options, see our electric sliding gate service.
Plan parking, pedestrian access and visitor waiting

Place your usual vehicle on the sketch, including the space needed to turn into the entrance and open its doors. If two vehicles share the drive, show both. The gate needs to work with the way you park rather than depend on everyone stopping at one exact spot every day.

Mark where a visitor stands to use an intercom and where a driver waits while the gate opens. Check whether deliveries, bicycles or a pushchair would bring someone beside the gathering panels. A separate pedestrian side gate may offer a better daily route where the site permits it.

Tell the surveyor about children and pets, and about any shared access. Small gaps and an apparently enclosed storage area still need assessment. Avoid choosing the panel layout first and treating pedestrian movement as a detail to solve after fabrication.
Assess the moving gaps between panels

Telescopic leaves create moving gaps between panels as well as at the closing edge and beside fixed objects. HSE’s powered-gate safety guidance specifically identifies hazards where telescopic leaves pass one another. The installer needs to assess the complete entrance and select protective measures for its actual use.

Ask the contractor to explain how the design addresses the panel storage area, accessible mechanisms and surrounding walls or fencing. A photocell across the entrance does not establish protection at every moving gap. Keep this discussion tied to the drawings and the completed installation checks.
Manual operation, servicing and future repairs

Before ordering, ask how an authorised user would gain access during a power failure. The answer must suit the selected mechanism and the property’s alternative entrances. Request a demonstration and written instructions at handover, including any restrictions on using the release.

Leave room for a service engineer to reach the drive equipment, guides and panel connections. A flower bed or cabinet added later can make a compact installation difficult to maintain. Ask which checks belong to the user and which require a competent engineer; follow the particular manufacturer’s maintenance instructions.

Record the panel hardware and operator models with the installation documents. Discuss parts availability and who will diagnose a problem involving both the sliding mechanism and automation. If the gate scrapes, moves unevenly or stops, report the observed behaviour rather than adjusting the panel connections yourself.
Compare the full quotation before choosing a finish

Request the same scope from each contractor: measured drawings, panel construction, finish, supports, foundations, drive equipment, access controls, protective measures and commissioning. Include removal of existing gates, electrical work, paving reinstatement and VAT where applicable. Use the installed gate cost guide to organise the comparison.

Separate the agreed work from provisional items and exclusions. Confirm who takes responsibility for coordinating the mechanical gate and its controls. Ask for the proposed installation sequence and any period when the entrance will be unavailable, rather than relying on a universal completion time.

The final choice should fit your usable entrance and the maintenance arrangements you can support. Choose the colour and infill after the survey establishes a workable layout. Keep the approved drawing with the quotation so a later change to panel numbers or hardware prompts a review of the space and work required.

Request views of the panels from inside the property as well as the road. Check how the overlaps, guides and back faces will look when the gate is open. If you want privacy, discuss sightlines through the panels at different angles instead of judging only a front-facing design image.
faqs: How much side space do telescopic gates need?

The selected mechanism, panel numbers, overlaps, supports and protective measures determine the required length and depth. Obtain a dimensioned drawing; a universal percentage of the opening width is not a reliable specification.
Can telescopic gates work on a sloping driveway?

The survey must establish levels across the opening and along the movement path. Ask the installer to assess the proposed system and manual operation rather than assume that sliding panels make any gradient suitable.
Are telescopic gates the same as cantilever gates?
No. Telescopic describes overlapping panels. Cantilever describes a support arrangement. Ask the contractor to identify the actual panel and support system in the proposal.

bi-fold-vs-sliding-gates-london.title: Bi-fold vs Sliding Gates for Short Driveways
bi-fold-vs-sliding-gates-london.description: Compare folding clearance and sliding run-back space without relying on a universal opening-speed or space-saving claim.
sections: Compare two different movement paths

Bi-fold leaves fold as they swing, reducing the depth occupied by some designs compared with a single full-length swing leaf. Sliding gates move alongside the opening and need a clear path beside it. Both arrangements need supports and space for their moving parts.

For a short drive, draw the parked vehicle, its doors, the gate’s entire movement and a pedestrian route. Ask the installer to mark the dimensions of the actual mechanism rather than applying a percentage saving from another product.
Check folding joints and side space

Folding designs need assessment around intermediate hinges and the area where the panels gather. Sliding designs need assessment along the run-back area and between the leaf and nearby walls or fencing.

If one sliding leaf will not fit beside the entrance, compare telescopic panels. More panels change the support, movement and maintenance requirements; they do not make the surrounding space irrelevant.
Include slopes and everyday access

Ground levels may interfere with a folding swing path or require changes to a sliding layout. Discuss drainage, parked-car position, visitors and bins. Ask what happens during manual release, particularly on a slope.

Opening time depends on the selected equipment, travel and safe operation. Do not choose a layout on a universal two-second promise. A demonstration should show the proposed arrangement, including its stopping and closing behaviour.
Get comparable proposals

Request drawings, product models, groundworks, protective measures and service arrangements for both options. Use the swing and sliding comparison for the broader layout questions, then compare the complete quotations using our installed gate cost guide.
Use a plan to compare what each design occupies

MeasureBi-fold proposalSliding proposal
Vehicle openingUsable gap with the folded panels and hardware in their final positions.Usable gap after the panel has travelled to its stored position.
Depth into the drivewayEntire folding and swinging envelope, not just the folded stack.Projection of the complete travel arrangement and protective separation.
Space beside the openingRoom occupied by folded leaves, supports and operating equipment.Full run-back length, supports and any cantilever tail.
Access for careHinges, linkages and operator servicing positions.Running gear, guides, drive and track where fitted.

Ask for both drawings at the same scale. Mark a parked car and the route a person uses beside it. A compact folded position does not show the space the gate passes through on the way there.
Compare realistic short-driveway situations

Where the boundary has little free length but the drive has some depth, a folding design may deserve assessment. Where the car occupies much of the depth but a clear side strip remains, a sliding proposal may deserve assessment. These are starting points for a survey, not recommendations for an unmeasured entrance.

If both dimensions are constrained, ask which requirement would have to change: parking position, opening width, supports or the gate arrangement. Include bins, meter cupboards and access to the garden before calling any storage area spare space.

Show the approach with the actual vehicle you use. A gate that clears the parked car may still be awkward during a tight turn. Do not choose between drawings that assume different parking positions or omit a vehicle projection.
Allow for ownership and maintenance access

Ask each supplier to identify the parts that need inspection and how an engineer reaches them. Discuss the effect of future paving, planting and fencing on that access. A design with more moving joints or panels needs a clear maintenance explanation, rather than a generic claim that all modern gates need little attention.

Compare finish care, supported replacement components and the documented manual-release arrangement. Ask for a demonstration of the complete operating sequence before handover. Keep the chosen layout with the service record so later changes to the drive can be checked against the gate’s actual movement.

underground-gate-motors-london.title: Underground Gate Motors for London Driveways
underground-gate-motors-london.description: Compare concealed swing-gate automation by drainage, hinge geometry, maintenance access and installation scope.
sections: What underground gate automation means

An underground swing-gate operator places much of the drive assembly in a foundation box near the hinge. This can reduce the equipment visible on the leaf, which may suit an entrance where appearance matters. Covers, release arrangements and other controls can remain visible.

The operator is one part of the entrance. The installer still needs to assess the gate, hinges, supports, exposure and movement. Concealing a motor does not make an unsuitable gate ready for automation.
Drainage and access belong in the design

Ask how the foundation box will drain at your property and who provides that work. Tell the installer about standing water and previous flooding. Discuss how the covers will remain accessible after paving, planting or resurfacing.

The quotation should identify excavation, foundations, cable routes, drainage and reinstatement. Ask how future maintenance or replacement can take place without unnecessary damage to the finished driveway.
Compare visible operators too

An above-ground arm may involve a different set of alterations and maintenance access. Compare both options against the hinge geometry, required opening angle and appearance of the whole entrance.

Request the proposed model and its suitability assessment. Voltage alone does not tell you whether a motor uses a hydraulic mechanism or what upkeep it needs. Follow the instructions for the specified equipment.
Keep release and handover practical

Ask for a demonstration of the actual manual release and how the leaf is controlled and secured afterwards. Keep the correct key and instructions accessible. Do not assume that every underground release sits in the same place.

Explore electric swing gates and our retrofit quotation guide. For an existing fault, arrange repair assessment before opening a motor enclosure.
What to include in a site survey

Provide photographs of the full entrance, the hinge areas and the finished ground from safe positions. Explain whether the gate is existing or new, whether the driveway will be resurfaced and where water collects after rain. Ask the installer to identify any further structural or drainage investigation needed before quoting.

Have the proposed drawing show the relationship between the gate pivot and the operator, together with foundation boxes, covers and cable routes. Request confirmation of the opening angle and the space the leaf occupies throughout travel. Do not assume that a concealed operator removes restrictions caused by a rising driveway.
Read the groundworks allowance carefully

WorkClarification to request
Excavation and foundationsWhat is included, and how will unexpected ground conditions be handled?
DrainageWhere does water go and who provides and maintains the arrangement?
Power and cablesWhich trade supplies the work and associated records?
Surface reinstatementWhat finish will match the existing drive and which area is included?
Future accessHow can covers be reached and equipment serviced after completion?

Compare those items with an above-ground option before deciding that concealment is worth the additional site work for your entrance. Keep appearance, repair access and the complete quotation in the same discussion.
Retrofitting and replacing underground equipment

For a retrofit, ask whether the existing hinges, posts and gate construction can work with the proposed operator. Identify any lifting, alterations or temporary removal in the quotation. Include safe access arrangements for residents while the entrance is unavailable.
