Delivery driverWhether the vehicle is known in advance and who accepts the delivery.A safe waiting point and a way to contact the recipient.
Contractor or hired vehicleTime-limited access if supported, with a named approver.A process for an unexpected registration change.

Do not publish a broad permanent permission list simply to reduce administration. Ask the supplier to demonstrate adding, correcting and removing a registration using the proposed system. Agree which person handles a resident changing car at short notice.
Check the entry and exit sequence

Draw the vehicle approach, waiting point and path through the entrance. Explain whether the same gate serves both directions and how a departing vehicle interacts with an arriving one. Include the busiest expected period rather than only a single test car on an empty driveway.

Ask the installer what triggers entry, how exit works and which component determines whether the gate can move safely. An accepted registration is permission to request entry; it is not confirmation that a person or another vehicle is clear of the gate.

Agree what happens when the network, recognition service or power is unavailable. Specify the authorised fallback and the person who receives a fault report. Avoid leaving an unexpected visitor with no way to call for help from the waiting position.
Make ownership and ongoing costs explicit

Request camera, processing and controller models, installation work, connectivity, licences and support terms in the quotation. Confirm which functions run locally and which depend on another service. Ask what changes if a subscription ends or the site changes its broadband provider.

The site operator should understand whether images, registrations and access events are retained, who can retrieve them and how deletion works. Record administration and account recovery arrangements at handover. Review access permissions when staff, residents or contractors leave, rather than allowing an old vehicle list to become the default.
faqs: Will ANPR read every plate?
Recognition depends on the camera, setup, approach, lighting, plate condition and supported plate formats. Test the actual proposal and agree a fallback.
Can cars enter without stopping?
Do not assume this. The design must provide a suitable approach and waiting arrangement while recognition and safe gate movement take place.
Does ANPR replace gate safety devices?
No. Permission to enter is separate from the protective measures and checks required for the powered entrance.

video-intercoms.title: Video Intercom Systems
video-intercoms.description: See and speak to visitors through a video-entry system specified for your gate, network and household.
sections: Choose where calls should ring

Discuss indoor monitors, phones and the people who need to answer. Confirm whether you need live video only, recordings or gate-position feedback. These functions vary by product and configuration.

Ask to see the proposed call and release sequence, including what happens when nobody answers. Plan deliveries and pedestrian access alongside vehicle entry.
Check the site connection

Survey power, cable routes, camera position, lighting and the required network connection. App access may depend on broadband or a mobile service as well as power at the entrance.

Confirm the exact interface with the gate controller. An intercom is not automatically compatible with every existing motor or control board. Changes need assessment and commissioning with the complete entrance.
Keep control of accounts and recordings

Agree who owns the administrator account, how residents are added and removed, and how recovery works. Confirm subscriptions, storage, recording settings and any remote-access charges.

Position cameras with neighbouring property and the public area in mind. Ask what privacy controls apply and obtain advice on the responsibilities of the operator where needed.
Compare the specified equipment

Use our intercom buying guide and documented product comparison. Confirm offered brands and model availability in your quotation.

Send photographs and any safely accessible equipment details when you discuss your entrance. Include installation, programming, user training and support in the agreed scope.
faqs: Can a video intercom work with my existing gate?
The installer needs to check the existing controller, wiring, condition and proposed interface. Compatibility cannot be promised from the motor brand alone.
Can I answer remotely?
Some configurations support remote calls through an app. Confirm the required connection, account, charges and failure arrangements for the specified model.
Does every system record visitors?
No. Recording, event logs, storage and subscriptions vary. Request the exact functions and privacy settings.

gsm-phone-entry.title: GSM Phone Entry Systems
gsm-phone-entry.description: Phone-based gate entry with the device, signal, SIM plan and user permissions checked for your entrance.
sections: Decide how phone entry should work

Discuss whether you want authorised callers to request opening, a visitor intercom that calls residents, or both. Ask how the proposed system identifies a caller and what happens if nobody answers.

A phone command does not confirm physical gate position. Agree how the household recognises a failed opening and how visitors obtain help.
Confirm the supported network and plan

Identify the exact device and the voice, SMS or data services it needs. Check the SIM provider’s requirements, tariff and account-expiry conditions. Calls or messages should not be described as universally free.

Read Ofcom’s mobile-network retirement guidance and obtain product-specific support information. The word GSM is often used for phone entry generally; confirm which network technology the proposed unit actually uses.
Survey signal and fallback access

Test the proposed service at the equipment location. Plan the power supply, antenna and cable route. A phone on a different network is not a complete signal test for the installation.

Phone entry may avoid dependence on home Wi-Fi, but it still depends on its own network, equipment and power. Agree a fallback for outages and confirm any backup maintenance.
Hand over account control

Record who owns the SIM and administrator account. Demonstrate adding and removing users using the supplied instructions. Confirm recurring charges and how support handles a change of phone number or ownership.

Read the phone-entry buying checklist or compare intercom options before you discuss your entrance.
faqs: Will any SIM work?
Check the model, supported network services and tariff terms together. Not every SIM or plan supports every gate device.
Is phone entry independent of power and broadband?
It may not need home broadband, but the gate and phone-entry equipment still need power and the required mobile service.
Are opening calls free?
That depends on how the product handles calls and the applicable tariffs. Confirm the charges rather than assuming a missed-call arrangement.

keypad-entry-systems.title: Keypad Entry Systems
keypad-entry-systems.description: Code-based gate access with user management, weather exposure and controller compatibility specified for your property.
sections: Choose how you will manage codes

Decide who needs permanent access and who should have temporary permission. Ask whether the selected keypad supports separate users, expiry or time windows. Those functions vary by model.

Avoid one shared code for everyone if you need to remove an individual’s access. Agree who can change settings and how you recover administrator control.
Place the keypad for its users

Discuss pedestrian and driver use, reach, lighting and the position relative to moving leaves. Visitors should not need to reach through a gate or stand in its movement path to enter a code.

Confirm the enclosure rating, operating conditions and mounting requirements for the actual product. There is no single weather rating we can promise for every proposed keypad.
Check the gate connection

The installer needs to assess the control interface, power, wiring and the existing gate’s condition. Code acceptance requests entry; it does not replace the protective measures needed for powered movement.

Ask what happens after repeated incorrect attempts, loss of power or a controller fault. Agree an authorised alternative for residents and visitors.
Include setup and handover

Request model details, programming, instructions and written support terms. At handover, practise adding and removing a user, replacing the initial codes and recovering access.

Compare video entry for visitors you want to speak with and our delivery-access guide for couriers. Then discuss your entrance.
faqs: Can delivery codes expire automatically?
Some models support expiry or time schedules. Specify that requirement and have the supplier demonstrate it before accepting the configuration.
How many users can I add?
Capacity and whether users have separate codes depend on the selected model. Confirm the limit in the product specification.
Can a keypad be fitted to an existing gate?
Compatibility, power, wiring and safe operation need assessment before installation.

pedestrian-side-gates.title: Pedestrian and Side Gates
pedestrian-side-gates.description: Pedestrian and side gates for London properties. Plan a usable walking route with the opening, lock, privacy and fitting details suited to your entrance.
sections: Plan the route people use every day

A separate pedestrian gate can let you enter without opening the vehicle gate. Start with who needs access: residents, visitors, deliveries, children or someone using a wheelchair or pushchair. Discuss clear opening space, thresholds, the approach and room to operate the gate.

Measure the route with the proposed handles, hinges and stops in place. A catalogue leaf width does not tell you the clear space available after fitting.
Choose privacy, handles and a lock together

Compare open-bar and boarded layouts, then decide how someone outside requests access and how a person inside exits. Confirm the lock, latch, handle height and any closer as part of the complete design. A closer changes how the gate moves and needs assessment with the chosen hinges and latch.

If you want electronic entry, discuss power, compatible locks, permissions and what happens during a power failure. Our access-control service can help you plan visitor entry. Shared entrances and escape routes need a site-specific assessment.
Match the gate to its supports

The installer should assess the existing wall, fence or posts before specifying the fixings. Agree the opening direction, finished ground level and drainage around the entrance. Choose materials and finishes that suit the surrounding boundary and the care you can provide.
Get a complete fitting quotation

Ask the quote to identify the gate, frame or posts, lock, handles, closer if proposed, removal work and making good. Include electrical work if required and request the care and warranty terms. If you are also replacing the driveway gate, ask for separate line items so you can compare the combined project.

Use our gate quotation checklist for the wider entrance work, or discuss your side-gate requirements.
A separate side gate or a wicket within the vehicle gate

A separate pedestrian gate has its own opening beside the vehicle entrance. A wicket is a smaller opening built into a larger gate leaf. Compare the clear width, threshold and approach of the actual products; the two arrangements do not provide the same walking route.

A separate gate may let pedestrians use an independent route, while a wicket can introduce a threshold and interactions with the larger gate. If a wicket is proposed within a powered leaf, ask the designer how its position and operation are assessed as part of the complete system. Do not assume it is suitable merely because it fits inside the frame.

Show who needs to use the entrance, including anyone with a wheelchair, pushchair or bicycle. Ask how the lock operates from each side and what happens in an emergency or power failure where electronic entry is fitted. Make those requirements part of the design before matching the appearance to the driveway gate.
faqs: Can the pedestrian gate match my driveway gate?
Discuss the material, finish, infill and visible fittings together. Matching options depend on the chosen range and the space available for the pedestrian entrance.
Can I use an intercom or keypad with a side gate?
It depends on the lock, access-control equipment, power supply and exit arrangements. Confirm the proposed components and failure behaviour before ordering.
What width should a pedestrian gate be?

Start with the people and equipment using the route, then assess the clear opening after fitting, approach space and threshold. Ask the installer to confirm suitability for your site and any applicable requirements.

industrial-security-gates.title: Industrial Security Gates
industrial-security-gates.description: Industrial gate systems for London sites. Discuss vehicle access, operating frequency, security requirements and aftercare before specifying equipment.
sections: Plan your entrance

Start with the site requirements: vehicle types, busiest arrival periods, clear opening, security objectives and routes for people on foot. Include delivery drivers and contractors who may not know the site.

Discuss the gate layout and access controls together. Existing ground conditions, supports, power and the space for vehicles to wait can affect the installation scope. A site survey should establish which arrangements are suitable before you order equipment.

If your brief requires a tested security rating or a named certification, ask for evidence for the exact proposed product and configuration. Do not treat the appearance of a gate or a general supplier claim as proof of that requirement.
Agree the installation scope

Vehicle movement

Assess the approach, turning room and clear opening for the vehicles using the entrance.

Operating demand

Give the installer the expected frequency and busiest periods so they can select equipment for the proposed duty.

Access control

Agree how staff, visitors and delivery drivers gain entry and who manages permissions.

Aftercare

Request written maintenance, fault-response and call-out terms. No response time applies unless it is agreed in the service contract.

Read HSE guidance on powered-gate responsibilities. For an existing fault, discuss a gate repair assessment. You can also compare the commercial entrance options.
Plan for the site’s busiest arrival period

Describe the vehicles that use the entrance, including the largest delivery vehicle and any combination of trailers or specialist equipment. Give the installer the operating hours and a picture of peak arrivals rather than only a daily average. Mark the place where a driver waits while permission is checked.

For a warehouse, include visiting drivers who do not know the site. For an industrial estate, identify different tenants and how visitors reach the correct occupier. For a depot, explain shift changes and occasions when several vehicles return together. These are planning scenarios; the survey must establish the actual arrangement.

Keep pedestrian entry and routes to reception visible on the layout. A driver should not need to leave a vehicle in a hazardous position to find the calling point. Coordinate the gate proposal with the site’s wider traffic arrangements and responsible person.
Compare gate types against operating requirements

OptionWhat to establish
Sliding gateRun-back space, support arrangement, foundations and separation from people.
Swing gateComplete swept area, supports and conflicts with waiting or turning vehicles.
Folding arrangementThe specified movement envelope, gathered panels and maintenance access.
Barrier alongside other measuresThe vehicle-control purpose and any separate perimeter or pedestrian requirements.

Ask for product and operating-duty information for the specified equipment. Do not infer a security rating, impact resistance or ability to cope with peak demand from the word industrial. If a rating forms part of the brief, match the evidence to the exact configuration being supplied.
Manage installation and handover as a site operation

Agree vehicle diversions, temporary access, pedestrian arrangements and the person coordinating the work. Explain any deliveries or operations that cannot be interrupted. Identify the responsibilities of the gate contractor, electrical contractor and site team before agreeing the programme.

At handover, request user instructions, equipment details, completed checks and training for the people who will operate or manage the entrance. Record who administers permissions and who responds to a fault. Agree maintenance and support in writing, including charges and any stated response terms.

Keep the site layout under review if traffic patterns, tenants or pedestrian routes change. A gate selected for an earlier arrangement should not be assumed suitable for a materially different operation without assessment.
faqs: Can you quote for a gate with a specified security rating?
Share the requirement with the enquiry. The proposed product and configuration need supporting evidence, and availability must be confirmed before a quotation promises a particular rating.
Is emergency call-out cover included?
Ask for the available support arrangements, charges and response terms in writing. Installation does not establish an automatic emergency-service agreement.
What should we prepare for the survey?
Provide the site layout, vehicle types, operating hours, access requirements and any known constraints. Identify who will approve the specification and look after the system after handover.
